title: Dedicated throughput degradation mitigation and longtail remediation plan
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: During a multi-region traffic burst on 2025-02-18 we observed sustained throughput degradation in several Dedicated pools. Root cause analysis identified an autoscaler policy interaction with newly deployed kernel scheduling heuristics that caused excessive scale-down and delayed scale-up under bursty workloads. This ticket captures the rapid mitigations we applied, the postmortem findings, and a set of engineering and product action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-18 09:12 UTC: Alert triggered (dedicated-pool-#7 p95 latency > 600ms) via Console alerting (route: dedicated-pool-ops).
2025-02-18 09:18 UTC: Triage call started. Initial hypothesis: new kernel scheduling heuristics (deployed 2025-02-17) increased per-request latency and reduced throughput under long-tail sequences.

2025-02-18 09:23 UTC: Autoscaler logs examined. Observed aggressive scale-down due to windowed CPU utilization falling below threshold after coordinated short bursts; scale-up lag of 45-120s because cooldown set to 90s and batching backlog underestimated.

2025-02-18 09:30 UTC: Emergency mitigations applied: increased min replicas for impacted pools (+30%), temporarily disabled scale-down for 10 minutes, and activated temporary surge pool (hotfix tag: surge-20250218).

2025-02-18 09:47 UTC: Traffic partially routed to hosted fallback for non-enterprise customers to reduce pressure on Dedicated pools while preserving enterprise SLA-customer traffic inside dedicated pools.
2025-02-18 10:15 UTC: p95 latency returned to acceptable range for critical pools; all mitigations remained in place while analysis continued.

2025-02-19 14:00 UTC: Root cause investigation completed: interaction between scheduler changes and autoscaler windowing plus a mis-tuned cooldown and scale-down multiplier exposed a regression for bursty workloads.
2025-02-24 11:00 UTC: Postmortem doc published and remediation PRs opened.
mitigations: Temporary: raised min_replicas on affected dedicated pools by 30% (surge-20250218) to provide headroom for bursts.
Temporary: disabled aggressive scale-down (scale_down_disabled=true) for 15 minutes post-detection to avoid oscillation.
Traffic routing: implemented emergency failover rules to route low-SLA or test traffic to hosted API for 2 hours.
Hotfix: reverted the specific kernel scheduling micro-optimization that reduced batch packing efficiency under sequence-length variance (revert PR #1293).
decisions: Do not revert autoscaler architecture — the problem is policy config and observability gaps, not the autoscaler codebase.
Adopt a predictive scaling add-on for dedicated pools that uses request-rate derivative and recent prefix-cache hit ratios rather than simple CPU windows.
Introduce a permanent 'surge pool' option for enterprise tenants that can be toggled via Console for planned events.
Require canarying of kernel/runtime changes against synthetic burst profiles before fleet-wide rollout.
Bound scale-down aggressiveness: change default scale-down multiplier from 0.5 to 0.75 and increase cooldown to 120s for dedicated pools by default.

ENG: add synthetic burst e2e tests in performance CI that replicate sequence-length variance and prefix-caching effects (owner: Arjun Rao, due: 2025-03-07) - CI job: perf/dedicated-burst
ENG: revert kernel micro-optimization and add regression unit test (owner: Elena Novak, due: 2025-02-25) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1293
PM/Design: add surge pool UX to Console with on/off toggle and expected cost estimate (owner: Maya Ortiz, due: 2025-03-14) - spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Surge+Pool+Spec

SRE: tune alert thresholds and add a p95 request-rate derivative alert to detect imminent scale pressure (owner: Grace Lee, due: 2025-02-28) - dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/8dedicated/pool-health
ENG/QA: run a controlled canary for autoscaler policy change against a 3-day business-hour window and measure fallback rate (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2025-03-04)
Security/Compliance: review surge pool billing controls and RBAC gating for toggling surge pools (owner: Arjun Rao, due: 2025-03-11)
